question.prompt: When a certain unfair die is rolled, an even number is \(3\) times as likely to appear as an odd number. The die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers rolled is even?

solutions.explanation:
Let \(p\) be the probability of an odd result. An even result has probability \(3p\), so \(p+3p=1\) gives odd probability \(1/4\) and even probability \(3/4\).

A sum is even exactly when the two rolls have the same parity. Independence gives
\[
\left(\frac14\right)^2+\left(\frac34\right)^2=\frac1{16}+\frac9{16}=\boxed{\frac58},
\]
choice E.
solutions.title: Separate same-parity cases
